subject: Culture
title: Retirement Across Cultures
description: A quick, practical guide to Retirement Across Cultures.

hook.text: Americans throw retirement parties. Japanese workers get a formal ceremony called taishoku. Others just keep working.

buildup.text: Retirement as a concept barely existed before the 20th century. Most people worked until they died.

discovery.text: Germany created the first state pension in 1889. Bismarck set the age at 70—when few people lived that long.

twist.text: In many African and Asian societies, elders never 'retire.' Their role shifts from worker to advisor.

climax.text: Retirement is a modern invention solving a modern problem: what do you do when your body outlasts your job?

punchline.text: Retirement is barely a century old.

quiz.question: Which country created the first state pension system?
